title: Turn an arbor press plate to the slot that backs the hub, set the pulley on it and press its shaft out
instruction: Press the shaft out of the red pulley hub on the arbor press.
context: Industrial machinery mechanics and machinists press shafts, pins and bushings out of pulleys and gears on an arbor press, turning its plate so the slot under the ram clears the shaft while backing the hub (O*NET 49-9041.00 Industrial Machinery Mechanics; 51-4041.00 Machinists). Board press tasks drive bushings, bearings and dowels in with drivers or a die; none sets a press plate to back the work so a part can pass through it. Here the narrow slot stops the shaft and the wide one drops the hub.
setup: Positions are object centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left (negative toward the right arm); z is height above the table top. Table: wood top, about 110 x 130 cm, arm bases 61 cm apart (y +30.5 and -30.5) on its near edge; nothing else on it. Arbor press, bolted down: dark grey steel column 6 x 4 x 37 cm tall (x 24 to 30, y -17 to -13) and head 6 x 15.5 x 4 cm (x 24 to 30, y -17 to -1.5, z 33 to 37). Ram: black steel bar 2.4 x 2.4 x 25 cm running up through the head on the axis x 27, y -3, its face at z 20 at the top of its stroke (it hangs about 1 cm lower), sliding down 11.4 cm to a stop 1 mm above a seated hub, 20 g with a light return spring (25 N/m); blue steel handle 7.8 x 1.8 x 3.0 cm tall on the bar's near face (x 18 to 25.8, y -3, z 23 to 26). Press plate: grey steel 14 x 14 x 1.5 cm, 100 g, top at z 5.5, turning with light drag on a dark grey post 2 x 2 x 4 cm at x 27, y +3; a slot runs in from the middle of three edges to 3 cm from the pivot: 1.4 cm wide on the -y edge (under the ram at the start), 3.0 cm on the -x edge, 5.4 cm on the +y edge; the +x edge is plain. A quarter turn anticlockwise seen from above brings the 3.0 cm slot under the ram. Orange steel grip tab 1.8 x 1.8 x 3.0 cm tall on the plate's +x +y corner, at x 32.7, y 8.7. Stand: light grey block 6 x 6 x 5 cm at x 17, y -19, fixed. Pulley: red steel hub 4.4 x 4.4 x 3.0 cm tall with a 2.4 cm square bore, 120 g, on the stand (z 5 to 8); yellow steel shaft 1.8 x 1.8 x 7.0 cm, 8 g, in the bore, bottom flush with the hub bottom, top 4 cm above the hub, a press fit that moves only under a steady push of about 4 N. All square to the table edges.
scoring: Open both grippers, then use a top photo and a ruler. Dropped: hub on the table or off it = 0. Turned (T): the 3.0 cm slot is under the ram, plate within 0.05 rad of a quarter turn (4 mm at the tab). Seated (S): hub flat on the plate (tilt at most 3 degrees, 2 mm across the hub; bottom within 2 mm of the plate top), shaft centre within 3 mm of the ram axis. Pressed (P): shaft top at most 5 mm above the hub top, driven there by the ram; more than 1.2 cm of shaft travel at any time without the ram face on the shaft top (pushed by a hand, hub lifted off it) voids P for the run. 1.0: T, S, P, ram face at least 3 cm above the hub, all still for 1 s. 0.5: T and S. 0.25: T only. Otherwise 0: the 1.4 cm slot (it stops the shaft), the plain edge or the 5.4 cm slot (the hub falls through) under the ram. A hub held up, on the stand or tilted is not seated.
reset_notes: Press the shaft back until its bottom is flush with the hub bottom, stand the pulley on its stand, turn the plate back so the 1.4 cm slot is under the ram and let the ram rest at the top of its stroke. Mark the stand and the plate's start on the table before the first trial. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid-body approximation: the press fit is a stiff damper on a slide (no press force or bore wear; the shaft sinks under 1 cm alone in 3 minutes), the pinion lever is a handle on the ram, and the ram has a light return spring. The simulator scores the last step without opening the grippers, so a hub whose bottom is more than 2 mm above the plate counts as not seated. Keeping hands from under the ram is a real-trial rule the scorer cannot see.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (Right arm picked the hub off its stand and dropped it on the table); demo: 1.0 (Turned the plate, set the hub on it, pressed the handle, and backed off)
